policy.status: Preregistered finite diagnostic; hypotheses are not pass conditions or route-proof labels.

cohorts.label: weapon only
cohorts.hypothesis: Control: weapons and shared stat picks only; decline all items.

cohorts.label: uncurated legal items
cohorts.hypothesis: Control: take the first legal item or chest choice without coordination.

cohorts.label: speed
cohorts.hypothesis: Hypothesis only: movement speed and moving attack-speed convert into late output.

cohorts.label: chain
cohorts.hypothesis: Hypothesis only: real-death explosions and root-local amplification form a chain route.

cohorts.label: HP/contact
cohorts.hypothesis: Hypothesis only: health, contact procs and pressure convert incoming contact into output.

cohorts.label: item-amplified firepower
cohorts.hypothesis: Hypothesis only: weapon modifiers and own proc power become the primary output.

cohorts.label: pickup feedback
cohorts.hypothesis: Hypothesis only: fuel, pickup bullets and pickup radius close a kill-to-output loop.

driver.writes: none; returns a normalized public step input vector

itemPolicy.scattered: Uncurated means choose the first legal offered array entry; it is not a guarantee of zero synergy.
itemPolicy.priority: Choose the first eligible, affordable offered item on the cohort list whose owned count is below both its native cap and cohort cap.
itemPolicy.noMatch: For priority cohorts, decline or skip rather than taking an off-route item.
itemPolicy.weaponOnly: Decline core rewards, chest choices and paid items; use the shared stat policy.
itemPolicy.dependencyAndSlotRules: All legality, dependency, uniqueness and price rules remain game-owned.

weaponSelection.rule: Among accepted, affordable offers, prefer an unowned type by shared rank; if all offered types are owned, prefer the lowest current tier by shared rank.
weaponSelection.purchasesPerRest: Keep buying the highest-ranked legal affordable weapon until the current row has no legal affordable offer.

rewardPolicy.coreAndChest: Priority cohorts take the first matching legal option; scattered takes the first legal array entry; weapon-only declines.

reserveAndSpend.itemPurchasesPerRest: Exhaust all useful legal affordable offers; no artificial one-item cap.
reserveAndSpend.weaponPurchasesPerRest: Exhaust all legal affordable offers, including fusion helpers; no artificial one-weapon cap.

rerolls.timing: After exhausting the initial rows, reroll once only if no useful legal affordable item remains and the current actual reroll price is affordable.
rerolls.afterReroll: Exhaust useful legal affordable items and weapons in the new rows; do not reroll again at this rest.
rerolls.stoppingRule: Skip the one reroll if any useful legal affordable item remains, if game reroll validation rejects the attempt, or if its actual price exceeds cash.

stepCaps.timeoutMeaning: Harness-only finite guard. It is never written into Game time, HP, deadline or RNG.

forbidden: source patch when an action API is missing

attribution.directItemDamage: Missing from the current public observation API; win/loss alone must not be called item-led damage attribution.
attribution.bossDamage: Only sampled positive boss-HP decreases are observable; no per-source attribution is claimed.

determinismReplay.compare: canonical JSON hash of the complete run record and per-wave records

policy.finiteOutcome: Run exactly 21 primary simulations in runOrder, then one replay; no tuning iteration.

offerAudit.interpretation: Offer rows, prices and public preview results are observed at row creation. With six occupied slots and every weapon at Tier II or higher, no Tier-I offer can merge and there is no empty slot; only a same-ID/same-tier fusion can free a slot. Rows without any Tier-I offer cannot supply a missing partner regardless of cash or future shop luck. This does not prove wallet scarcity or a failed DPS check.

runs.routeLabelEvidence: Cohort labels describe preregistered acquisition policies; they do not prove a route formed or caused output.
runs.actualItemDamageAttribution: missing: the public read-only API exposes weapon/item projectile metadata and damage-source parameters but no per-hit source ledger
